front: What is the optimal linear discriminant vector in Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis for default prediction?
back: The projection vector that maximizes the between-group to within-group variance ratio: w* = S_W^{-1}(mu_1 - mu_2), where S_W is the pooled within-class covariance matrix and mu_1, mu_2 are the class mean vectors.
basis: Fisher Rayleigh quotient maximization theorem in L01

front: What are the five financial ratios in Altman's (1968) original manufacturing Z-score model?
back: X1 = Working Capital / Total Assets, X2 = Retained Earnings / Total Assets, X3 = EBIT / Total Assets, X4 = Market Value of Equity / Book Value of Total Liabilities, X5 = Sales / Total Assets.

front: What are the empirical classification zones for the original 1968 Altman Z-score model?
back: Safe Zone: Z > 2.99; Grey (Inconclusive) Zone: 1.81 <= Z <= 2.99; Distress Zone: Z < 1.81.

front: How does the Altman private-firm revision (Z') modify variable X4?
back: X4 is replaced by Book Value of Equity divided by Total Liabilities, and its coefficient is recalibrated from 0.60 to 0.420, because private firms lack observable equity market valuations.
basis: Altman (1983 revision of 1968 framework)

front: How does Altman's accounting Z-score relate empirically to structural Merton distance-to-default models?
back: Bharath & Shumway (2008) empirically demonstrate that Merton distance-to-default is not a sufficient statistic for default; accounting ratios from the Z-score framework add significant incremental predictive power.
basis: Bharath & Shumway (2008, p. 1341)

front: How are the post-default recovery rate and Loss Given Default (LGD) defined?
back: Recovery rate R = V(tau + delta) / D, where V is recovered economic value and D is contractual allowed default claim. Loss Given Default is LGD = 1 - R.
basis: Contingent claim accounting definition in L02

front: What is the contractual seniority ordering of corporate debt claims in Chapter 11?
back: 1. Super-priority DIP financing (§ 364); 2. First lien secured bank debt; 3. Second lien secured notes; 4. Senior unsecured debt and trade credit; 5. Subordinated debentures; 6. Preferred and common equity.
basis: Bankruptcy Code § 507 statutory priority hierarchy in L02

front: Why do empirical recovery rates for senior secured first lien debt exhibit a bimodal distribution?
back: Recoveries cluster near 100% (full par recovery) in successful reorganizations or prepackaged Chapter 11s, or at 10% to 30% in distressed piecemeal asset liquidations.
basis: Replicated across Moody's and S&P corporate default empirical studies

front: Why is Loss Given Default (LGD) procyclical with respect to aggregate default rates?
back: Macroeconomic recessions trigger widespread defaults while simultaneously depressing collateral asset resale values and industry liquidity, causing default frequency and loss severity (LGD = 1 - R) to spike together.
basis: Theorem 1.2 Chebyshev association theorem under macroeconomic credit cycle drift in L02

front: What is the economic distinction between contractual subordination and structural subordination?
back: Contractual subordination is established by indenture agreement where junior debt agrees to defer payment to senior debt. Structural subordination arises from corporate entity architecture: operating subsidiary debt has direct priority access to operating assets before dividends can flow upstream to pay holding company debt.
basis: Asset partitioning and corporate separateness doctrine in L02

front: What is the Absolute Priority Rule (APR) in Chapter 11 bankruptcy?
back: Codified in 11 U.S.C. § 1129(b)(2)(B)(ii), APR requires that in a non-consensual plan confirmation (cramdown), no junior class may receive or retain any property unless senior dissenting classes are paid in full.
basis: 11 U.S.C. § 1129(b)(2)(B)(ii) statutory cramdown standard

front: Why does Bankruptcy Code § 1121 debtor exclusivity give old equity strategic bargaining leverage?
back: Debtor management has the exclusive right to file a plan for up to 18 months. Contesting cramdown threatens litigation delay and administrative fee burn, creating a deadweight loss that senior lenders pay to avoid.
basis: Theorem 1.1 strategic delay bargaining game in L03

front: What is the equilibrium equity carve-out in Chapter 11 strategic delay bargaining?
back: K* = (1 - gamma)(beta * T + C_L), where gamma is senior bargaining power, beta is monthly administrative burn, T is delay duration, and C_L is direct litigation cost. Both parties strictly prefer this consensual APR violation over litigated cramdown.
basis: Theorem 1.1 generalized Nash bargaining solution in L03

front: What voting thresholds are required under Bankruptcy Code § 1126(c) for an impaired class of creditors to accept a plan?
back: Class acceptance requires at least two-thirds (66.67%) in dollar amount of allowed claims voting, and more than one-half (>50%) in the number of voting creditors.
basis: 11 U.S.C. § 1126(c) statutory voting requirement

front: What did the U.S. Supreme Court rule in Czyzewski v. Jevic Holding Corp. (2017) regarding structured dismissals?
back: Bankruptcy courts cannot approve non-consensual structured dismissals that distribute estate assets in violation of statutory priority by skipping over intermediate priority wage/tax claimants.
basis: Czyzewski v. Jevic Holding Corp., 137 S. Ct. 973 (2017)

front: What does Section 316(b) of the Trust Indenture Act of 1939 prohibit?
back: It prohibits impairing or modifying an individual bondholder's right to receive payment of principal and interest when due without 100% unanimous consent of every holder outside of Chapter 11.
basis: 15 U.S.C. § 77ppp(b)

front: Why does Section 316(b) create a coordination failure in out-of-court debt exchange offers?
back: If other creditors tender and forgive debt, the firm becomes solvent; non-tendering holdouts retain their original claims and get paid 100 cents on the dollar, making holding out an individually dominant strategy.
basis: Theorem 1.1 public bondholder holdout game in L04

front: How does an exit consent overcome the public bondholder holdout dilemma?
back: Tendering bondholders simultaneously vote to strip non-core protective covenants from the old indenture, leaving holdouts with illiquid, subordinated stub paper and making tendering the dominant strategy.
basis: Theorem 1.2 exit consent equilibrium in L04

front: What was the resolution split for troubled firms documented by Gilson, John & Lang (1990)?
back: Out of 169 distressed firms (1978-1987), approximately 52.7% (89 firms) successfully restructured out of court, while 47.3% (80 firms) filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy petitions.
basis: Gilson, John & Lang (1990, p. 320)

front: According to Gilson, John & Lang (1990), how does debt composition affect out-of-court restructuring success?
back: Firms owing a higher fraction of debt to commercial banks (49.0% vs 37.5% for filers) are significantly more likely to succeed out of court, because concentrated bank lenders resolve information asymmetry and coordination frictions far better than dispersed bondholders.
basis: Gilson, John & Lang (1990, p. 328)

front: What is the definition and role of the fulcrum security in distressed debt restructuring?
back: The most senior debt tranche that is partially covered by reorganization enterprise value; it absorbs the marginal value fluctuation and receives substantially all reorganized common equity under the Plan of Reorganization.
basis: Definition 1.2 and Theorem 1.1 in L05

front: How does the fulcrum security migrate as debtor enterprise value increases across scenarios?
back: The fulcrum tranche index k*(V) is a monotonically non-decreasing step function of EV: as enterprise value expands, senior tranches become fully covered and the fulcrum migrates strictly down the capital structure.
basis: Theorem 1.1 partition monotonicity in L05

front: How is an intermediate debt tranche payoff mathematically isomorphic to an option spread on enterprise value?
back: Tranche payoff Pi_k(V) = max(0, min(D_k, V - C_{k-1})) is identical to a bull call spread on enterprise value: long a call struck at prior debt C_{k-1} and short a call struck at total cumulative debt C_k.
basis: Problem P1 bull call spread equivalence in L05

front: How does a distressed debt investor establish a statutory blocking position in Chapter 11?
back: By acquiring more than 33.34% of allowed claims by dollar amount in an impaired class, wielding a negative veto to block consensual class acceptance under Bankruptcy Code § 1126(c).
basis: 11 U.S.C. § 1126(c) voting standard in L05

front: How are Multiple on Invested Capital (MOIC) and annualized IRR calculated for a secondary distressed debt purchase?
back: MOIC = Expected Recovery / Purchase Cost = Expected Recovery Rate / Price. Annualized compound IRR = MOIC^{1/T} - 1, where T is the holding period in years.
basis: Definition 1.3 compound return accounting in L05
